title: straddle.yaml
description: Distributable feature/app unit that spans firmware + browser. See docs/plans/straddles.md.

schema_version.description: Schema revision; reserved for future evolution.

name.description: Canonical <org>/<repo> identity. Matches the github path.

prefix.description: Short identity used as symbol prefix, include subdir, browser import name. May be empty (only spangap-core uses the empty prefix by convention).

version.description: Semver-ish version string. Pin-only for now; no version-range solver.

stub.description: Immutable firmware identity: the short lowercase stub name (e.g. 'reticulous'). Defines WHAT is running, not what it's running on — not a hostname, not user-editable. Reserved as the future state-directory prefix (so multiple firmwares' state can coexist on one SD card). Desugars to CONFIG_SPANGAP_FW_STUB and is exposed read-only to the browser as fw.stub. Layers by dependency order like any kconfig value — the straddle highest up the dependency tree (the one being built) wins; spangap-core, deepest, loses.

display_name.description: Immutable firmware identity: the user-facing proper name shown in the leftmost menu (e.g. 'Reticulous'). Desugars to CONFIG_SPANGAP_FW_NAME, exposed read-only as fw.name. Dependency-order layered; the built straddle wins.

banner.description: Immutable firmware identity: a one-line description / slogan / motto (e.g. 'Reticulum mesh networking for the masses!'). Desugars to CONFIG_SPANGAP_FW_BANNER, exposed read-only as fw.banner. Dependency-order layered; the built straddle wins.

default_hostname.description: Compile-time DEFAULT for the MUTABLE s.net.hostname (e.g. 'reticulous'). Unlike stub/display_name/banner this seeds a user-settable value (what it's running ON), not immutable identity. Desugars to CONFIG_SPANGAP_FW_HOSTNAME, which seeds s.net.hostname on first boot. Dependency-order layered; the built straddle wins.

firmware.description: Firmware-half path relative to manifest dir. Omit for default 'idf'. Use '.' when the manifest dir IS the firmware project root (buildable straddles).

browser.description: Browser-half path relative to manifest dir. Omit for default 'browser'.

platforms.description: Which build platforms this straddle's firmware half supports. Today: just idf.

requires.description: Other straddles this one HARD-depends on — every build that pulls in this straddle must also pull in these. Each entry is '<org>/<repo>' optionally followed by '@<ref>' (tag/branch/SHA). A missing requires: target is a build error.

additional_installs.description: Other straddles to ALSO stage whenever this one is in the build — default-on extras pulled in transitively, droppable with --without/--no-X. Unlike requires:, absence is NOT an error: a listed straddle that isn't on disk (or was dropped) is pruned silently. This is the 'pull in the kitchen sink' knob, kept deliberately rare — an aggregator/app straddle uses it to assemble a device's feature set; most straddles list nothing here. An entry is either a plain '<org>/<repo>' spec (unconditional) or the object form { install:, when: }, which stages install: only when the when: straddle is itself in the resolved closure — the edge expresses a conjunction ('this extra makes sense only when X is ALSO here') without dragging X in. Gates are evaluated to a fixpoint, and a when: straddle dropped by --without takes the gated extra with it (unless something else still reaches it). Source code that integrates with a thus-pulled straddle must still gate its call sites on the auto-generated CONFIG_STRADDLE_<UPPER_NAME> (or the CONFIG_SPANGAP_LCD/CONFIG_SPANGAP_WEB shortcuts) so a --without drop compiles away cleanly.

install.description: The straddle to stage — same '<org>/<repo>[@ref]' spec as the plain-string form.

when.description: Gate: stage install: only when this '<org>/<repo>' straddle is in the resolved closure (same vocabulary as the when: on init:/start:/browser_register: hooks). Omit for an unconditional entry (equivalent to the plain-string form).

start.description: START-phase hooks (the legacy free-function form of a Service onStart — see services: for the object form): bare-hardware bring-up the platform itself depends on. The generator wraps each in an adapter Service and runs it in the serviceRunStart() walk, as the FIRST thing in app_main — BEFORE spangapInit(), i.e. before fs/storage/log/cli even exist. This is the band for a board straddle to power a peripheral rail before spangap-core's fs_mount_sd() touches the SD bus, register the display/touch HAL before spangap-lcd's lcdInit(), etc. CONTRACT (the strict inverse of init:): a start hook runs on bare hardware — it must NOT use info()/warn()/dbg(), storage*, fs_*, or ITS (none are up yet); raw peripherals only (GPIO, power rails, pin mux, bus CS parking, HAL/driver registration that later init: hooks consume). Ordering is the same dependency-topo walk as init: (a board lands early because its dependents require: it); within one straddle, hooks fire in listed order. Same entry shape and `when:` gating as init:. By convention a start hook is named xStart (e.g. tdeckStart), mirroring the xInit convention of init:.

call.description: Start function symbol, e.g. 'tdeckStart'. A plain global `void <name>()` (default C++ linkage) defined in this straddle's firmware half — same convention as init:'s xInit. The dispatcher forward-declares it with C++ linkage and calls it, so no header wiring and no `extern "C"` wrapper is needed (a C-linkage symbol from a .c file would need one to match).

when.description: Optional gate: emit this hook's call only when the named straddle ('<org>/<repo>') is in the staged build set. Resolved at generation time against the staged set — when the straddle is pruned the call is simply NOT written (no #if), so the hook symbol is never referenced and -ffunction-sections/--gc-sections drops it along with its references into the now-absent dep. Use the same '<org>/<repo>' vocabulary as additional_installs (e.g. 'spangap/spangap-lcd'). Omit for an unconditional hook.

init.description: INIT-phase hooks (the legacy free-function form of a Service onInit — see services: for the object form) this straddle wants the buildable to run automatically, AFTER spangapInit() (the platform foundations) — the post-infrastructure band, contrast start: above. spangap-inside collects these across the staged set and, in the generated staging/spangap_init_dispatch.gen.cpp, wraps each in an adapter Service run in the serviceRunInit() walk, in two bands: first spangap's own platform components (core, net, web, lcd) in that fixed order, then every other straddle in dependency-topo order (a straddle inits after the straddles it requires:). There is no per-hook order knob — a straddle that must come up after another declares it in requires:/additional_installs: and the topo walk handles it; everything in the straddle band can already assume the platform band is up. Within one straddle, hooks fire in listed order (and legacy init: hooks register before services: entries). The buildable ships no main.cpp — app_main is generated; from then on, staging a straddle that declares init: is enough to have it initialize — no consumer edit. Each entry's `call` is a plain global `void <name>()` defined in this straddle's firmware half (the generated dispatch emits its own C++-linkage forward declaration, so no header wiring and no `extern "C"` is needed). By convention an init hook is named xInit.

call.description: Init function symbol, e.g. 'sshdInit'. A plain global `void <name>()` (default C++ linkage) defined in this straddle's firmware half — the same convention every straddle's xInit() already follows. The dispatcher forward-declares it with C++ linkage and calls it, so no header wiring and no `extern "C"` wrapper is needed (a C-linkage symbol from a .c file would need one to match).

when.description: Optional gate: emit this hook's call only when the named straddle ('<org>/<repo>') is in the staged build set. Resolved at generation time against the staged set — when the straddle is pruned the call is simply NOT written (no #if), so the hook symbol is never referenced and -ffunction-sections/--gc-sections drops it along with its references into the now-absent dep. Use the same '<org>/<repo>' vocabulary as additional_installs (e.g. 'spangap/spangap-lcd'). Omit for an unconditional hook. This is the finer-grained twin of how a whole straddle's hooks already appear only when it is staged — it lets one straddle's hook ride on ANOTHER straddle's presence.

browser_register.description: BROWSER-side registration hooks — the browser-half parallel to init:. spangap-inside collects these across the staged set (same init_order as the firmware boot registration) and generates, into a buildable's browser half, src/boot/straddles.gen.ts: a default-export registerStraddles() that imports each hook's `call` symbol from this straddle's browser package and invokes it, in order. It also injects a `file:../../<repo>/browser` dependency into the buildable's browser package.json so the import resolves under node_modules. The buildable loads the generated function ONCE from its hand-written boot/modules.ts (import registerStraddles from './straddles.gen'; registerStraddles()) — the browser analog of the firmware's generated boot registration. From then on, staging a straddle that declares browser_register: is enough to surface its UI (menu pane, etc.); no consumer edit. Only emitted into buildables that have a browser half, and only for staged straddles that themselves have a browser half. Same `when:` gating as init:. By convention the symbol is named register<Prefix> (e.g. registerWg) and is exported from <pkg>/modules/<repo>.

call.description: Exported registration function to import and call, e.g. 'registerWg'. A named export of this straddle's browser package, conventionally from the modules/<repo> entry point (see `module`). Its job is to register the straddle's UI (menu panes via useMenuStore().register, etc.). The casing is not derivable from the repo name (e.g. duckdns exports registerDuckDns), which is why it is declared explicitly.

module.description: Import subpath within this straddle's browser package (the part after '<pkgname>/'), resolved through the package's exports map. Defaults to 'modules/<repo>' (e.g. wg -> 'modules/wg'), which is the convention every current browser half follows. Override only for a non-standard module layout.

when.description: Optional gate: emit this hook's import+call only when the named straddle ('<org>/<repo>') is in the staged build set. Resolved at generation time — when the gating straddle is pruned the registration is simply not written, so its panel never bundles. Same vocabulary and semantics as init:'s when:.

kconfig.description: Sdkconfig default lines this straddle contributes to the build — the road by which a NON-buildable straddle (typically a board, e.g. hw-lilygo-tdeck) supplies Kconfig VALUES that another non-buildable straddle's component Kconfig DEFINES (LoRa/SD/LCD pins, etc.). spangap-inside collects every staged straddle's lines into staging/sdkconfig.spangap-fragments, which bootstrap.cmake layers into SDKCONFIG_DEFAULTS between the platform defaults and the buildable's own sdkconfig.defaults. Precedence is the init order: platform band first, then the straddle band in dependency-topo order, then the buildable itself last (the building straddle wins among fragments); the buildable's sdkconfig.defaults and CLI overrides win over all of it. Each item is emitted verbatim as an sdkconfig line, so the RHS (=y, ints, hex, "quoted strings") is preserved exactly. The peripheral straddle still owns the option's schema/help/range in its component Kconfig — this only sets the value. Two different straddles setting the same symbol is warned about (silent last-wins otherwise). An item may instead be a `when:`-gated group (when: <org>/<repo>, set: [lines]) whose lines apply only when that straddle is staged in the build — so a board can set a peripheral's Kconfig values (e.g. LoRa/audio pins) without them warning as unknown symbols in a build that omits the consuming straddle.

when.description: Straddle slug <org>/<repo>; the group's set: lines are applied only when that straddle is staged in the build.

services.description: Boot-registered Service objects (see spangap-core service.h) this straddle contributes. The modern replacement for start:/init: free-function hooks: instead of declaring a bare `void xInit()` symbol, declare a Service SUBCLASS and the generated boot code constructs it and appends it to the ordered registry (serviceRegister) at the straddle's init_order position. The object participates in a boot phase purely by overriding that phase's virtual (onStart pre-spangapInit / onInit post-spangapInit) — the generator never learns which phases a class overrides. spangap-inside emits, per entry, a per-straddle trampoline TU (staging/components/<repo>/spangap_services.gen.cpp) that #includes the class header and defines spangapService_<Class>() { serviceRegister(new <Class>()); }; the generated app_main forward-declares and calls that symbol in boot order. The trampoline rides SPANGAP_CONDITIONAL_SRCS (the straddle's CMakeLists must already compile ${SPANGAP_CONDITIONAL_SRCS} in SRCS — the same list conditional/ code uses), and the class header must be on the component's include path (e.g. a public include/ header, or a conditional/<name>/include header when the class is gated). Class requirements: external linkage, GLOBAL (no namespace — the codebase disambiguates by symbol prefix), default-constructible with an ECOSYSTEM-FREE ctor (member init only — storage/fs/log/cli/ITS are NOT up when ctors run at the very top of app_main). An LcdApp is a Service, so an on-device app is just a services: entry. Same `when:` gating as init:. Within one straddle, legacy init: entries register before services: entries.

settings.description: Declarative settings — a list of CONTRIBUTIONS to one shared settings tree. Every node in that tree may hold both key/value rows and sub-nodes (rows render first, then the children as navigation entries), and no node is owned: a contribution names a path with `at:`, every intermediate node on the way is conjured, and several straddles contributing at the same path simply concatenate their row blocks. spangap-inside lowers the collected tree into THREE generated surfaces from this single source: (1) the on-device LCD node (lcdSettingsContribute + lcdSetting* calls, gated on spangap-lcd being staged), (2) the browser node fragment (serialized into straddles.gen.ts and interpreted at runtime by spangap-web's NodePane renderer), and (3) the persisted storage defaults (storageDefault() for every binding row carrying a `default:` whose key starts with `s.`). Two conventions carry the expressiveness: firmware publishes FINISHED STRINGS (any derived display value — signal wording, composed counters, formatted percentages — is written to an ephemeral key as the exact text to show, and gate keys are truthy/empty; UIs never compute or compare), and firmware VALIDATES IN SENTINEL HANDLERS (a mutation lands on a command key, the owning task validates it and on rejection writes a human-readable reason to `<cmd>.error`, cleared on the next successful write; UIs submit and display, they never validate).

class.description: The Service subclass to construct and register, e.g. 'MapsApp'. GLOBAL (no namespace), external linkage, default-constructible with an ecosystem-free ctor. Its instance is `new`'d once at boot and lives forever. The generated trampoline symbol is spangapService_<class>.

header.description: The header (as written in an #include "...") that declares the class, e.g. 'maps_app.h'. Resolved against this component's include path — a public include/ header, or a conditional/<name>/include header when the class is when:-gated on <name>. No '<prefix>.h' magic: name it explicitly.

when.description: Optional gate: construct+register this service only when the named straddle ('<org>/<repo>') is in the staged build set. Resolved at generation time — when the gating straddle is pruned, neither the trampoline TU nor its registration call is emitted, so the class (and its header) need not exist in that configuration. Same vocabulary and semantics as init:'s when: (e.g. an LcdApp service gates 'when: spangap/spangap-lcd').

at.description: Where this contribution lands, as an ordered list of path segments from the Settings root. EVERY segment names a node, and the last one is where the rows go — there is no leaf/container distinction, because a node holds rows AND children. Intermediate nodes are conjured; no node is owned, so several straddles may contribute rows at the same path and their blocks concatenate in the global order rule. Each segment carries `id` (the stable lowercase slug — the merge key, and the node's path id on both surfaces), and optionally `label` (long name), `short` (the LCD header name; defaults to the label) and `order`. The FIRST contributor (in straddle init order) to supply a label/short/order for a node wins; a later conflicting value is ignored with a build-time warning.

rows.description: The rows this contribution adds to the node, top to bottom. Each row is an object whose kind key (section/caption/switch/slider/text/dropdown/value/button/list) carries the spec, plus the optional `when_kconfig`/`when_key`/`order` modifiers.

order.description: Orders this contribution's row block among the other blocks at the same node. Follows the global rule: blocks with `order:` first, ascending; blocks without it after them, in (straddle init order, declaration order).

settingsScalar.description: A settings integer, either literal or { kconfig: CONFIG_NAME, default: N } — resolved at build time from the staged set's collected kconfig: fragments, so a board can size a control to its hardware. The default applies when no straddle sets the symbol.

settingsBound.description: A slider bound: a settingsScalar, or { key: <storage key>, default: N } — read from a value the device publishes at run time rather than fixed at build time. Use it when the firmware knows the real limit and the build does not, e.g. a capability detected on the hardware itself. The default applies until the key exists.

settingsAction.description: What a button does. Three kinds, accepted anywhere an action is: settings buttons, dialog buttons, and a collection's per-item buttons. Template substitution inside an action is `{field}` replacement only — no expressions, no fallbacks; anything fancier is a string the firmware publishes.

edge.description: Write 0 first, then the value, forcing a change event past the storage actor's dedup. Needed by command flags that may be left set by an attempt that did not complete — without the edge, the second press writes the value the key already holds, nothing changes, and no subscriber ever fires.

reboots.description: The write reboots the device. The web client then runs the shared reboot-wait behaviour (close the session, wait, reload) and the LCD shows a modal notice, instead of every caller carrying its own choreography.

dialog.description: A confirmation or choice. NO input fields, ever — that is what `form` is for. Every button closes the dialog; a button with no `do:` is a cancel. Buttons nest actions, so a choice tree is dialogs of buttons of sets.

settingsForm.description: The one dialog that carries inputs, because it fronts a command sentinel. `fields` are ordinary binding rows carrying `field:` instead of `key:` — values are collected locally, not written per keystroke. Submitting serializes the field object as JSON to `cmd`. The owning task validates: while `<cmd>.error` is non-empty the form stays open showing the reason. Success is the TARGET CHANGING — inside a collection that is the array key, so the form closes when the mutation is observed; a standalone `form:` action has no target to watch, so it closes on submit and a late rejection surfaces on the pane that owns the sentinel.

cmd.description: The command sentinel this form submits to. Required for a standalone `form:` action; inside a collection's `add:` it defaults to `<cmd>.add`, so the sentinel family stays derived from the collection's one `cmd` name.

when_kconfig.description: Emit this row only when a Kconfig symbol is set — `CONFIG_X`, or `!CONFIG_X` for only when it is NOT set. Gates all three lowered surfaces at once: the LCD row, the browser row, and the storageDefault() seeding — so a build that gates a feature out has no key for it in storage and no mention of it in either UI. Resolved at generation time against the staged set's `kconfig:` fragments, exactly like a settings scalar's `{ kconfig: … }` form, and with the same limit: a symbol nobody set in a straddle.yaml reads as unset here, even if the compiler sees it set from sdkconfig.defaults or `spangap menuconfig`. A feature meant to ship as a build variant therefore declares its symbol in a `kconfig:` block, which is the one place both halves of the build can see it.

when_key.description: Show this row only while a storage key is TRUTHY (non-empty, non-zero). Purely runtime — both surfaces subscribe to the key — and truthiness only: never an equality test, because the firmware publishes gate keys as truthy/empty exactly so the UIs do not have to compare. Inside a collection's item editor or a form the key may use `{field}` substitution to reference a sibling field, e.g. `when_key: "{dhcp}"`.

order.description: Orders this row among its siblings. Declaration order is the default and is usually what you want; where an order is stated it wins, per the global rule (ordered first ascending, unordered after in arrival order).

field.description: Bind to a form/item-editor field of this name instead of a storage key.

searchable.description: Render as a type-to-filter picker rather than a plain select. For option lists too long to scan (timezones, countries).

value.description: A read-only row showing whatever string the key holds. The firmware publishes the FINISHED text — the UI never formats, composes or compares.

copyable.description: Web: a click-to-copy affordance and select-all styling (for hashes, addresses, URLs). LCD: no change beyond the existing focus/marquee behaviour.

list.description: A collection: an array-of-objects in storage, rendered as titled item rows with an editor, add forms, removal and optional reordering. The UI NEVER mutates the array — every mutation is a write to a command sentinel under `cmd`, and the owning task is the only writer.

key.description: The array key. Items are per-field objects under it; a packed multi-field string does not bind, so an owner adopting this block migrates its storage shape.

id.description: The field identifying an item in sentinel payloads and status keys.

item.description: Row title, a `{field}` template over the item.

subtitle.description: Optional second line (monospace, dimmer), same templating.

status.description: Optional ephemeral key template (e.g. "rns_tcp.peer.{id}") holding a status pill as packed "text|color" — the firmware publishes both halves finished.

empty.description: Caption shown when the array is empty.

orderable.description: Enable reordering. The UI writes the complete id order to `<cmd>.order` as a comma-joined list; the firmware treats it as a PREFERENCE PERMUTATION — reorder recognized ids into that relative order, ignore unknown ids, leave unmentioned ids in place — which keeps it idempotent and benign under concurrent edits.

cmd.description: Sentinel base. `<cmd>.add` takes a JSON item, `<cmd>.remove` an item id, `<cmd>.set` a JSON item including its id (the OLD id when the id field itself was edited), `<cmd>.order` the id list. Rejections land on `<cmd>.error`.

add.description: One or more add entry points, each a form submitting to `<cmd>.add`.

confirm.description: Confirmation text, `{field}`-templated over the item. Omit for no confirmation.

actions.description: Per-item action buttons. `{field}` templates in the action resolve against the item, and `{id}` against its id field.

edit.description: The item editor — rows binding item-relative `field:`s, rendered as a dialog on web and a sub-pane on the LCD. Semantically a child node over the item's key scope, so every row feature works here, `when_key` with `{field}` included. Commits go through `<cmd>.set`.

candidates.description: Scan-and-adopt: an ephemeral array the owning task publishes, rendered like list rows. Picking one opens the collection's first add form, prefilled. Runtime contract: when the pane holding this clause stops being visible the runtime clears the refresh target key, so no straddle carries a visibility timer for "stop scanning on leave".

item.description: Row template over whatever fields the task publishes, pre-rendered bars and lock markers included.

map.description: candidate-field → add-form-field renames. Same-name fields map implicitly; this is only for the ones that differ.
